{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) as the base framework for all sink modules, leveraging its binder abstraction.",
    "Follow the existing s-c-s module conventions (auto-configuration, configuration metadata, channel adapters) for new and ported modules.",
    "Ported XD modules will be adapted to the s-c-s programming model (annotation-based configuration, MessageChannel-based APIs) rather than a 1:1 copy of XD code.",
    "Kinesis module will use AWS SDK v2 (Kinesis Producer/Consumer libraries) for integration with AWS Kinesis streams.",
    "Job DSL integration will be implemented as an opt-in module on top of Spring Batch DSL, exposed through s-c-s stream/job lifecycle hooks.",
    "Flink processor will be built on Apache Flink's DataStream API, integrating FlinkML-style abstractions for streaming ML (e.g., feature extraction, online statistics, model scoring).",
    "Java 17 will be the source/target version, matching Spring Framework 6.0 requirements.",
    "Build system: Apache Maven (multi-module reactor), consistent with existing s-c-s conventions.",
    "Testing stack: JUnit 5, Spring Test, embedded Kafka test binder, AssertJ, Mockito.",
    "Each module delivered as its own Maven sub-module with dedicated unit, integration, and smoke tests."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A single experienced developer (familiar with Spring, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring XD, Flink, and AWS SDK) performs all work; no onboarding overhead.",
    "Reference XD source code is available and the existing s-c-s repository structure is in place — no large-scale refactoring of the parent project is required.",
    "Reasonable local development environment (IDE, Maven, Docker for integration tests) is already configured.",
    "Cloud/infra costs (e.g., live AWS Kinesis) are not part of the effort; testing uses Testcontainers/embedded equivalents.",
    "Scope per user story is interpreted as: one production-quality module/feature with tests and basic reference documentation (no extensive user guides or marketing material).",
    "No production-level performance tuning or benchmarking beyond basic sanity is included.",
    "Job DSL implementation provides core orchestration primitives sufficient to demonstrate job definition and workflow creation (not full parity with a production orchestrator).",
    "Flink ML processor covers a representative set of streaming ML abstractions (feature extraction, online scoring) — not an exhaustive MLlib port.",
    "Activities are sequential in estimation but can be parallelized in practice; effort (work-hours) is reported, not calendar duration.",
    "No localization, security hardening beyond Spring defaults, or large-scale dependency upgrades are included."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Project setup, codebase analysis and scaffolding",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing s-c-s repository layout, parent POM conventions, module structure, CI configuration, and XD reference modules. Add placeholder Maven sub-modules for each new/ported module and align them with s-c-s conventions (auto-config, spring.factories/imports, configuration metadata).",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Kinesis sink module (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Implement a new s-c-s sink module targeting AWS Kinesis. Includes AWS SDK v2 integration, Kinesis sink configuration properties, Message-to-PutRecord conversion, batching, error handling, retry/backoff, and auto-configuration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Port Log sink module from XD (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD Log sink module to s-c-s as a sink: review XD implementation, adapt to s-c-s MessageChannel API, expose configurable log format/level, register auto-configuration, and align naming/properties with s-c-s conventions.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Port field-value-counter sink module from XD (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD field-value-counter module to s-c-s: maintain per-field value counts in a managed store (in-memory + optional Redis), expose counters via metrics/actuator, and adapt to s-c-s sink contract.",
      "most_likely_effort": 14
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Port aggregate-counter sink module from XD (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD aggregate-counter module to s-c-s: implement time/marker-based aggregation windows, configurable store (in-memory + Redis), reset/expiration semantics, and metric exposure.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Port gauge sink module from XD (U6)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD gauge module to s-c-s: implement a single-value gauge that stores the most recent (or computed) numeric value and exposes it as a metric via Spring Actuator.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Port rich-gauge sink module from XD (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD rich-gauge module to s-c-s: implement a multi-attribute gauge (value, average, max, min, count, time-to-live) with configurable storage and actuator exposure.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Job DSL integration (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Introduce a Job DSL option into s-c-s: design the DSL grammar, integrate with Spring Batch/job infrastructure, expose stream-to-job transitions, provide tasklet/step/job definitions via DSL, and document the workflow orchestration use cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Flink-based streaming ML processor (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Develop a s-c-s processor that delegates to Apache Flink, exposing streaming ML abstractions (feature extraction, windowed statistics, online scoring, simple model serving hooks). Includes Flink cluster lifecycle integration, s-c-s bridge (Flink operators consuming/producing s-c-s messages), and example ML pipelines.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Unit testing across all modules",
      "activity_description": "Write JUnit 5 unit tests for every module developed in A2–A9: configuration binding, message conversion logic, store/metric behavior, DSL parsing, and Flink operator functions. Use Mockito and AssertJ.",
      "most_likely_effort": 36
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Integration and smoke testing",
      "activity_description": "End-to-end tests using embedded Kafka test binder, Testcontainers (Redis, LocalStack for Kinesis, embedded Flink mini-cluster) to verify each module behaves correctly within a s-c-s pipeline, plus integration tests for the Job DSL and Flink processor paths.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Reference documentation",
      "activity_description": "Produce concise reference documentation for each new/ported module and feature: module overview, configuration properties, sample pipeline definitions, and a short overview of the Flink ML processor and Job DSL usage patterns.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "Build, dependency management and CI updates",
      "activity_description": "Update parent POM and BOM with required dependencies (AWS SDK v2, Flink, Spring Batch DSL), wire new sub-modules into the reactor, ensure consistent plugin configuration, and update CI workflow to build and test the new modules.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 316
  }
}

The specification describes:
1. The Spring Framework background (context)
2. 8 user stories (U1-U8)

Let me break down what needs to be developed:

**U1**: Kinesis module - a sink module for streaming pipeline. This is a new AWS Kinesis sink module for Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s).

**U2**: Port Log module from XD to s-c-s repo as a sink module.

**U3**: Job DSL - integrate job DSL as an option for creating workflows and orchestrating jobs.

**U4**: Port field-value-counter module from XD to s-c-s repo as a sink module.

**U5**: Port aggregate-counter module from XD to s-c-s repo as a sink module.

**U6**: Port gauge module from XD to s-c-s repo as a sink module.

**U7**: Port rich-gauge module from XD to s-c-s repo as a sink module.

**U8**: Flink processor - process data using Flink processor for streaming machine learning abstractions.

So we have:
- 1 new sink module (Kinesis)
- 5 modules to port from XD (Log, field-value-counter, aggregate-counter, gauge, rich-gauge)
- 1 Job DSL integration
- 1 Flink processor for ML

- Use Spring Cloud Stream framework as the base
- Follow existing XD module patterns for porting
- Use Spring Boot for new modules
- Use Flink's streaming APIs for the Flink processor
- Java 17+ as the language
- Maven or Gradle for build (assume Maven based on Spring conventions)
- Testing using JUnit 5 and Spring Test
- Use the existing s-c-s architecture and module conventions

**Assumptions:**
- The developer has access to existing XD source code for reference
- The developer is familiar with Spring Cloud Stream and Spring XD
- A single developer performs all the work
- Standard development environment with IDE
- Reasonable existing test infrastructure in s-c-s
- 5 ported modules have similar complexity, differing in business logic
- AWS SDK for Kinesis integration
- No major architectural changes needed

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) as the base framework for all sink modules, leveraging its binder abstraction.
Follow the existing s-c-s module conventions (auto-configuration, configuration metadata, channel adapters) for new and ported modules.
Ported XD modules will be adapted to the s-c-s programming model (annotation-based configuration, MessageChannel-based APIs) rather than a 1:1 copy of XD code.
Kinesis module will use AWS SDK v2 (Kinesis Producer/Consumer libraries) for integration with AWS Kinesis streams.
Job DSL integration will be implemented as an opt-in module on top of Spring Batch DSL, exposed through s-c-s stream/job lifecycle hooks.
Flink processor will be built on Apache Flink's DataStream API, integrating FlinkML-style abstractions for streaming ML (e.g., feature extraction, online statistics, model scoring).
Java 17 will be the source/target version, matching Spring Framework 6.0 requirements.
Build system: Apache Maven (multi-module reactor), consistent with existing s-c-s conventions.
Testing stack: JUnit 5, Spring Test, embedded Kafka test binder, AssertJ, Mockito.
Each module delivered as its own Maven sub-module with dedicated unit, integration, and smoke tests.
assumptions: A single experienced developer (familiar with Spring, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring XD, Flink, and AWS SDK) performs all work; no onboarding overhead.
Reference XD source code is available and the existing s-c-s repository structure is in place — no large-scale refactoring of the parent project is required.
Reasonable local development environment (IDE, Maven, Docker for integration tests) is already configured.
Cloud/infra costs (e.g., live AWS Kinesis) are not part of the effort; testing uses Testcontainers/embedded equivalents.
Scope per user story is interpreted as: one production-quality module/feature with tests and basic reference documentation (no extensive user guides or marketing material).
No production-level performance tuning or benchmarking beyond basic sanity is included.
Job DSL implementation provides core orchestration primitives sufficient to demonstrate job definition and workflow creation (not full parity with a production orchestrator).
Flink ML processor covers a representative set of streaming ML abstractions (feature extraction, online scoring) — not an exhaustive MLlib port.
Activities are sequential in estimation but can be parallelized in practice; effort (work-hours) is reported, not calendar duration.
No localization, security hardening beyond Spring defaults, or large-scale dependency upgrades are included.
